answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small, time-bound deposit before it earns any reward, with the stake slashed when independent peers prove a fake identity. Like a sparrow that must sing at dawn to prove it survived the night, an agent proves liveness through repeated, costly work rather than cheap claims. The deposit is tied to a cipher-based identity key that cannot be copied without losing the stake, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits while honest agents keep their earnings.
